concepts.title: State of Agent Governance Decision Rights
concepts.research_question: Who decides, funds, operates, assures, contains, decommissions, and remains accountable for a concrete deployed agent?
concepts.original_data_required: SURVEY-001 role-by-decision matrix, matched deployment cases, verified role at source time, organization and deployment context, outcome denominators, and public-source lineage.
concepts.interview_requirement: At least 24 rights-cleared interviews, including eight matched organizations with two or more roles and at least four negative or contested cases.
concepts.survey_requirement: SURVEY-001 threshold: at least 300 eligible respondents with role-specific, organization, geography, industry, and cell-suppression floors.
concepts.geography_coverage: At least three publishable regions; no global estimate; original-language work where required.
concepts.expected_evidence_contribution: First OFF decision-rights baseline linking role, authority, evidence, budget, handoff, and outcome for disclosed samples.
concepts.methodological_risk: Selective OFF recruitment, uneven role cells, duplicated organizations, title inflation, matched-case survivorship, and inference from responsibility to belief.
publication_timeline_sequence: frozen release and later trend eligibility
concepts.relation_to_annual_state_of_executive_th: Flagship cross-role governance chapter and reusable decision-rights measure; annual product must quote role-specific bases and not generalize beyond the recruited sample.

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: Unrestricted foundation grant or cross-functional professional association
sponsorship.conflict_risk: Identity, security, consulting, insurer, or platform sponsors could influence which role is framed as buyer or owner.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Funding category, OFF ownership, advisory and investment relationships, recruitment channels, and sponsor limits.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Protocol and analysis pre-registered; sponsor cannot select participants, edit instrument, access analysis, approve findings, or control release.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: Public report and aggregate appendix only; no identities, contacts, recordings, row-level data, or small cells.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Null, adverse, cross-role, and sponsor-inconvenient findings remain publishable.

concepts.title: Agent Authorization Implementation Registry
concepts.research_question: Which identity, credential, delegation, monitoring, and shutdown patterns are implemented, and what bounded outcomes and failures are reported?
concepts.original_data_required: Validated deployment-level registry with architecture, version, scale, autonomy, identity granularity, credential lifecycle, delegation, revocation, task utility, incidents, cost, interoperability, failure, and corroboration fields.
concepts.interview_requirement: At least 20 implementation interviews across 12 organizations, including technical and control owners and at least six failed or abandoned deployments.
concepts.survey_requirement: SURVEY-002 threshold: at least 120 validated records across 40 organizations, four industries, three regions, and 20 failed or abandoned cases.
concepts.geography_coverage: Three or more regions with deployment, data, incident, and regulatory geography separated.
concepts.expected_evidence_contribution: Comparable implementation patterns, negative cases, denominator quality, and clear separation of reported from independently corroborated outcomes.
concepts.methodological_risk: Heterogeneous deployments, vendor and maturity selection, incomplete denominators, confidential failures, version drift, and causal overinterpretation.
concepts.relation_to_annual_state_of_executive_th: Provides the implementation evidence layer beneath annual executive positions and exposes where recommendation frequency lacks outcome support.

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: Standards body, audit association, or unrestricted research foundation
sponsorship.conflict_risk: Pay-to-include, favorable architecture comparison, and vendor lead generation.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Funding, platform, implementation, vendor, and contributor relationships.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: No paid inclusion or sponsor-selected cases; independent eligibility and corroboration.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: Public deidentified registry only; no confidential diagrams, identities, or submissions.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Failed, abandoned, and unfavorable cases remain eligible.

concepts.title: Human Oversight and Monitor Reliability in Agent Workflows
concepts.research_question: When do approval, monitoring, hard limits, and shutdown controls improve oversight, and when do they create delay, fatigue, false confidence, privacy burden, or task failure?
concepts.original_data_required: SURVEY-003 plus a prospective subset with approval events, latency, overrides, task outcomes, monitor false positives, missed events, shutdown use, user burden, and privacy review.
concepts.interview_requirement: At least 18 interviews across approvers, operators, security monitors, workflow owners, privacy or affected-user representatives, and audit leaders.
concepts.survey_requirement: At least 200 eligible respondents across 30 workflows and 15 organizations; causal or effectiveness claims require a separately registered prospective field-study subset.
concepts.geography_coverage: At least two regions for pilot; expand only with comparable workflow and consent conditions.
concepts.expected_evidence_contribution: Separates perceived burden from logged outcomes and creates credible positions for the currently ineligible approval-versus-monitoring debate.
concepts.methodological_risk: Unknown missed events, self-report bias, monitoring changes behavior, privacy intrusion, incomparable workflows, and confounding between risk and control intensity.
concepts.relation_to_annual_state_of_executive_th: Supplies a recurring oversight-burden and control-confidence module, reported separately from evidence strength and market adoption.

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: Independent safety or human-factors research foundation
sponsorship.conflict_risk: Monitoring or workflow vendors may equate product use with safety and minimize privacy burden.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Product, research, recruitment, and analysis relationships.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Independent privacy, protocol, and statistical review; no sponsor-defined success metric.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No user-level data, logs, identities, or unpublished safety events.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Null, adverse, burden, and privacy findings remain publishable.

concepts.title: Global Agent Governance Legal and Operating Atlas
concepts.research_question: How do jurisdiction, language, industry, infrastructure, and operating context change agent identity, delegated authority, audit, privacy, and accountability practice?
concepts.original_data_required: Verified local public sources, original-language records, regulator and operator interviews, legal-status fields, implementation cases, and separate speaker, organization, market, study, incident, event, and regulatory geographies.
concepts.interview_requirement: At least three local interviews and two organizations per published jurisdiction or region, including operator and legal or regulatory perspectives.
concepts.survey_requirement: No prevalence survey required for the first edition; any quantitative comparison follows SURVEY-001 subgroup floors and a regional sampling plan.
concepts.geography_coverage: Wave one: Singapore, Japan, EU/EEA, UK, and Australia; separate protocols for Africa, Latin America and Caribbean, and Middle East and North Africa before synthesis.
concepts.expected_evidence_contribution: Corrects global-label substitution, adds non-English evidence, distinguishes law from guidance and practice, and identifies genuinely local implementation differences.
concepts.methodological_risk: Translation error, legal overgeneralization, policy-heavy sampling, elite bias, incomparable regions, rapidly changing law, and one-source representation.
publication_timeline_sequence: comparative atlas only after scope alignment
concepts.relation_to_annual_state_of_executive_th: Provides region-specific chapters and prevents the annual product from labeling standards with global applicability as evidence of global executive representation.

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: International professional association or neutral foundation
sponsorship.conflict_risk: Sponsor may promote one jurisdiction, member base, or legal interpretation.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Regional, institutional, membership, translation, and legal-review relationships.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Local reviewers validate language and law, not sponsor-preferred conclusions.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No contacts, private translations, interview files, or small cells.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Critical local findings and non-comparability remain explicit.
